source_text: Cui hunc statum dedi, ut ei nolenti nemo noceret externus, sed sponte capesseret vel peccatum vel iustitiam vel praemium vel reatum.
pass_a_gloss: To whom I gave this status, that no external one would harm it unwilling, but of its own accord it would take up either sin or justice or reward or guilt.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: I gave it this condition: no outsider could harm it against its will; instead it would freely embrace either sin or justice, either reward or guilt.

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
